patternEvidence: Apple Native App Pattern Atlas: macOS 27.0, build 26A5416b, August 22, 2026. Notes master-detail, Calendar toolbar roles, separate settings, scoped sheets. Clock and Reminders styling is an interpretation, not a direct captured implementation claim.
actionCountDefinition: Visible idle buttons, inputs, and disclosure controls, including navigation but excluding macOS window chrome.

spikes.title: Clock Face
spikes.rationale: Clock-style timer owns the window; a short inline summary opens rules and mode instead of exposing a setup form.
spikes.strength: Clearest idle-to-active transition and the least setup noise in a full window.
spikes.tradeoff: Large timer uses space that a compact menu-bar utility may not need.

spikes.title: List First
spikes.rationale: Reminders-style source list treats the block list as a stable object and the session as its primary action.
spikes.strength: Scales naturally to several block lists with familiar sidebar navigation.
spikes.tradeoff: Sidebar and duplicate list affordance add weight for a single-list user.

spikes.title: Session Library
spikes.rationale: Notes-style master-detail layout places ad-hoc and recurring sessions in one browsable library.
spikes.strength: Scheduled and one-off focus share a clear mental model.
spikes.tradeoff: Mixes session templates and schedules; may imply persistent sessions that Zone does not yet model.

spikes.title: Menu Bar Essential
spikes.rationale: A small menu-bar panel has one primary action, a duration, and two descriptive navigation rows.
spikes.strength: Best fit for a menu-bar utility; low visual effort, every advanced setting one step away.
spikes.tradeoff: Rule and schedule management needs a deeper view or the main window.

spikes.title: Today Agenda
spikes.rationale: A Calendar/Reminders-inspired agenda positions an immediate session in the day next to scheduled work.
spikes.strength: Explains when focus happens and makes recurring sessions visible without a separate destination.
spikes.tradeoff: Calendar context competes with the simple need to start a timer.

spikes.title: One Outline
spikes.rationale: A single vertical document uses native disclosure rows for rules, session policy, and schedules.
spikes.strength: Every feature remains discoverable without a sidebar or button grid.
spikes.tradeoff: Expanded sections can become long; timer hierarchy is less distinctive.

spikes.title: Quiet Inspector
spikes.rationale: The timer has a quiet canvas; a standard contextual inspector reveals configuration only when needed.
spikes.strength: Lowest persistent visual density; strong separation between doing and configuring.
spikes.tradeoff: Inspector can feel excessive for three fields and requires more window width.

spikes.title: Clock Toolbar
spikes.rationale: Clock-like icon-and-label toolbar destinations replace a sidebar while keeping focus, schedules, and blocks reachable.
spikes.strength: Predictable navigation with native controls and no duplicated navigation links.
spikes.tradeoff: Three persistent destinations still consume space in a small utility.

ranking.reason: Best product fit: compact, one primary action, descriptive rows, no always-visible mode or pause form.
Best full-window companion: immediate comprehension, clear active state, configuration reduced to short links.
Simplest full-feature architecture without a sidebar; useful disclosure treatment.
Familiar navigation but less minimal than the top three.
Strong calmness; configuration feels slightly too distant.
Good for multiple lists, unnecessarily wide for the current single-list use case.
Useful if schedules become central, adds timeline structure today.
Elegant library model, requires a product concept not yet present in Zone.
